findings.why: The override unbinds MaxBalanceModule right after the base setup sets the 1000 cap. ModularCompliance.canTransfer then only consults CountryRestrictModule, so nothing limits any investor's balance.
findings.steps: setUp runs; agent calls token.mint(a1, 5000), which passes isVerified and canTransfer, so a1 holds 5000 against a cap of 1000. Any verified holder can also receive more than 1000 via transfer.

findings.why: With the module unbound, no per-identity cap is checked. a1 and a2 share identity idA, but together they can hold far more than 1000.
findings.steps: agent mints 1000 to a1 and 1000 to a2 (both under idA); both succeed, so identity idA holds 2000.

findings.why: Once MaxBalanceModule is removed from _modules, it no longer receives moduleMintAction, moduleTransferAction or moduleBurnAction. Its _IDBalance records stay frozen and diverge from real token balances.
findings.steps: agent mints 500 to b; token.balanceOf(b) is 500 but maxBalanceModule.getIDBalance(compliance, idB) is 0.

findings.where: MaxBalanceModule._getIdentity (used by moduleCheck, moduleMintAction and moduleTransferAction)
findings.why: _getIdentity returns the wallet address and never looks up the identity in the identity registry. Balances are therefore tracked per wallet, and two wallets of the same identity (a1 and a2, both under idA) each get their own 1000 cap.
findings.steps: agent mints 1000 to a1 (succeeds). agent mints 1000 to a2 (succeeds, since a2 is verified via idA's claim). Identity idA now holds 2000 tokens, above the 1000 cap. A normal transfer from b to a2 would also pass the check.

findings.where: Deployment._addModules (mint before modules are bound, then batchPreSetModuleState with balance 0)
findings.why: The override mints 800 tokens to b before MaxBalanceModule is bound. It then presets idB's recorded balance to 0 instead of 800. The module's record for idB no longer matches b's real balance. Any later transfer or burn of b's tokens subtracts from a recorded 0 and underflows.
findings.steps: setUp runs _addModules: mint(b,800) with no modules bound -> batchPreSetModuleState(idB,0) -> addModule. Then getIDBalance(idB)=0 while balanceOf(b)=800. Then b.transfer(a1,100) reverts in moduleTransferAction with an underflow on _IDBalance[idB]-=100.

findings.where: Deployment._addModules (mint before modules are bound, then batchPreSetModuleState with balance 0)
findings.why: Because idB's recorded balance is 0 rather than 800, the 1000 cap check lets idB receive up to 1000 more tokens. Identity idB can then hold 1800 tokens, which exceeds the 1000 cap.
findings.steps: After setUp: agent mints 1000 to a1 (the mint is allowed since a1 is within the cap). a1.transfer(b,1000): moduleCheck sees 0+1000 <= 1000 and passes, and moduleTransferAction records 1000. b now holds 1800 tokens against a cap of 1000.

findings.why: forcedTransfer moves balances with _transfer but never calls _tokenCompliance.transferred. MaxBalanceModule's _IDBalance is therefore not updated, so the sender identity keeps its old recorded balance and the receiver identity is recorded too low. Recovery goes through forcedTransfer, so it has the same problem.
findings.steps: mint 900 to a1 (idA record 900); agent forcedTransfer(a1, b, 900); token balances are a1=0, b=900 but the module still shows idA=900 and idB=0

findings.why: After a forced transfer or recovery the receiver's recorded balance is too low. Normal transfers and mints then pass the cap check against the stale record, so an identity can hold more than 1000 tokens.
findings.steps: mint 900 to a1; agent forcedTransfer(a1, b, 900); mint 1000 to b (module sees idB 0 + 1000 <= 1000); b now holds 1900 tokens, above the cap of 1000

findings.why: The override replaces the base configuration and sets the holding cap to the maximum uint256 instead of the issuer's 1000. The base version uses CAP = 1000, but the override never calls it.
findings.steps: Deploy with the override; maxBalanceModule._maxBalance[compliance] = 2^256-1 instead of 1000.

findings.why: With the cap at max uint256, every cap check in the module passes. An identity can therefore hold far more than 1000 tokens through normal mint and transfer calls.
findings.steps: agent calls token.mint(b, 5000), which passes isVerified and canTransfer. Then b transfers or receives more tokens, and the balance stays above 1000 with no revert.

findings.why: The module tracks balances per identity, but the shared cap for a1 and a2 (same identity idA) is effectively unlimited because the cap is max uint256. The combined holdings of the two wallets can exceed 1000.
findings.steps: agent mints 800 to a1 and 800 to a2. Both succeed, so identity idA holds 1600.
